The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For the group and cotangent conventions of [[def-rpm-h-poincare-charge-space]], the map $\mu:T^*\mathbb R^4\to\mathfrak g^*$ defined by $\langle\mu(x,p),(a,A)\rangle=\ell_{(a,A)}(x,p)$ is a smooth equivariant moment map and obeys

$$\{\ell_\xi,\ell_\eta\}=\ell_{[\xi,\eta]},\quad \{P^a,P^b\}=0,\quad \{J^{ab},P^c\}=\eta^{ac}P^b-\eta^{bc}P^a,$$

$$\{J^{ab},J^{cd}\}=\eta^{ac}J^{bd}-\eta^{ad}J^{bc}-\eta^{bc}J^{ad}+\eta^{bd}J^{ac}.$$

For each future massive shell $p_0=-E/c$, $E=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\mathbf p|^2}$, or nonzero future null shell with $m=0$ and $|\mathbf p|>0$, its Poincare charges descend to the global ray quotient. The induced dual action is $(P,J)\mapsto(\Lambda P,\Lambda J\Lambda^T+a\wedge\Lambda P)$. On the fixed-time slice $x^0=ct$, with physical position $q^i=x^i$, the boost component $B_i=J^{0i}=ct p_i-q^iE/c$ is explicitly time dependent and satisfies $\partial_tB_i+\{B_i,E\}=0$. These are mathematical identities; conservation is conditional on the stated free-shell evolution.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the referenced cotangent and symplectic-action conventions. Work on affine Minkowski spacetime with inertial coordinates $x^0=ct,x^1,x^2,x^3$ in metres, metric matrix $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and cotangent coordinates $(x^a,p_a)$, where each $p_a$ has SI momentum units. Fix the future cone as the timelike component containing the positive $x^0$ axis, equivalently $v^0>\lvert\mathbf v\rvert$. Let $SO^+(1,3)$ denote the determinant-one, future-cone-preserving Lorentz subgroup. Define the proper orthochronous Poincaré group and its multiplication by

$$G=\mathbb R^4\rtimes SO^+(1,3),\qquad (a,\Lambda)(b,L)=(a+\Lambda b,\Lambda L).$$

Its action on spacetime and the cotangent lift are $x'=\Lambda x+a$ and $p'=\Lambda^{-T}p$. The Lie algebra consists of pairs $(a,A)$ with $A^T\eta+\eta A=0$, bracket

$$[(a,A),(b,B)]=(Ab-Ba,[A,B]).$$

Use the library convention $\xi_M=\left.\frac d{ds}\right|_0\exp_G(-s\xi)\cdot z$. Thus the positive affine generator on spacetime is $Y_{(a,A)}(x)=a+Ax$, the fundamental field is its negative, and the cotangent-lifted positive field is $(a+Ax,-A^Tp)$. Pair the cotangent point with a Lie-algebra element by

$$\ell_{(a,A)}(x,p)=p_b(a^b+A^b{}_cx^c).$$

Define $P^a=\eta^{ab}p_b$ and $J^{ab}=x^aP^b-x^bP^a$. The equivalent dual pairing is $\ell_{(a,A)}=p_ba^b-\tfrac12J_{bc}A^{bc}$, where $A^{bc}=A^b{}_d\eta^{dc}$ and $J_{bc}=\eta_{bd}\eta_{ce}J^{de}$. Here $[P^a]=\mathrm{kg\,m/s}$ and $[J^{ab}]=\mathrm{J\,s}$. These are charge-space definitions on the full cotangent bundle; shell reduction and the moment-map identities are stated separately. No spin or particle model is included.

derivations.claim: By the canonical product bracket, $\{q_aE_a,p_1+p_2\}=E_a$ for each $a$, since $E_a$ is independent of position; also $\{t(p_1+p_2),p_1+p_2\}=0$. Hence $\{K,P\}=(E_1+E_2)/c^2$.

The Hamiltonian is $H=E_1+E_2+kr^2/2$, so $H/c^2-\{K,P\}=kr^2/(2c^2)>0$ whenever $r=q_1-q_2\ne0$. The required algebra relation in [L1] fails there. Since $k$ has units $\mathrm{kg/s^2}$, $kr^2/2$ is energy and the compared charges have matching units. This refutes this proposed free-boost construction only.

Assume countable choice ACω, as in [[def-countable-choice]], for the smooth cotangent-bundle carrier convention used by this page; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Let $\mathcal D$ be an open subset of the time-dependent tangent bundle $\mathbb R\times TQ$ of a finite-dimensional smooth manifold $Q$, and let $L:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. For fixed $t$, the **fibre derivative** is the map

$$\mathbb F L(t,q,v)=(t,q,p),\qquad p(w)=\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}L(t,q,v+sw),$$

as in [[def-fibre-derivative-and-legendre-transform-of-a-lagrangian]]. In induced coordinates $p_i=\partial L/\partial v^i$.

The Lagrangian is **regular** at $(t,q,v)$ when the velocity Hessian $(\partial^2L/\partial v^i\partial v^j)$ is invertible there; regularity gives only a local inverse branch. It is **hyperregular on a declared domain** when $\mathbb F L$ is a diffeomorphism from that entire domain onto an open subset of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$.

It is **almost regular on a declared domain $\mathcal D_0\subseteq\mathcal D$** when the following are all assumed: $\mathbb F L|_{\mathcal D_0}$ has constant rank; its image $N$ is an embedded submanifold of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$; its corestriction $\mathcal D_0\to N$ is a surjective submersion (its differential is surjective at every point); and every fibre of that corestriction is connected. These hypotheses are not consequences of singularity alone.

Assume countable choice ACω, as in [[def-countable-choice]], for the smooth cotangent-bundle carrier convention used by this page; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Fix a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,T)$ with signature $(-+++)$, as in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Here $T$ denotes the supplied smooth timelike field selecting the future cone, called $N$ in that geometric definition. Use the distinction among a spacetime, a worldline, a pointwise observer, an observer congruence, a tetrad and a chart given in [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. This definition does not make $g$ dynamical.

In this relativistic-particle model, $m>0$ is a fixed **primitive mass parameter** measured in kilograms, and $c>0$ is a fixed **primitive conversion parameter** measured in metres per second. They are parameters of the adopted physical formulation, not quantities derived by this definition. Coordinates $x^a$ in an SI chart have length units; a cotangent vector $p=p_a\,dx^a$ has units of momentum, $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, when all four coordinates are in metres. The canonical one-form $p_a\,dx^a$ therefore has action units $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Along a future-directed timelike curve with tangent $V=dx/d\lambda$, set $s:=\sqrt{-g(V,V)}$; then $d\tau=s\,d\lambda/c$, independently of the increasing regular parameter. The length action $-mc\int s\,d\lambda$ has action units. For a future unit observer $n$ and future causal covector $p$, define the model normal-observer energy and spatial momentum covector by

$$E_n(p):=-c\,p(n),\qquad q_n(p):=p+p(n)n^\flat,$$

where $n^\flat=g(n,\cdot)$. The restriction of $g^{-1}$ to covectors annihilating $n$ is positive definite, so it supplies the norm of $q_n(p)$. These are quantity definitions and unit conventions; they do not identify canonical momentum with mechanical momentum, assert that an apparatus measured these values, or establish a dynamical law.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $n$. Its cotangent bundle is

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units \([F]\) and \([G]\) has units \([F][G]/(\text{action})\). These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. The use of $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ is exactly the use in the smooth cotangent-bundle suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ and let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold. A finite family of smooth functions $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ defined on an open neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ is a **regular primary constraint family** on

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units \([\chi_a]\), then $u^a$ has units energy divided by \([\chi_a]\), so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

Use the signature $(-,+,+,+)$ throughout. In the flat case, **Minkowski spacetime** means the affine model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]: $A$ is an affine space, $\eta$ is a nondegenerate Lorentz form on its four-dimensional displacement space, and $C^+$ selects the future cone. In the curved case, a **background spacetime** means a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the metric and time orientation are fixed data, not dynamical unknowns here. No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the smooth subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. In the flat model these are affine curves into $A$ with tangent in the selected future timelike or null cone from [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]].

An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** is a chosen orthonormal frame field, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.

For a $C^2$ future-directed timelike worldline $x:I\to M$ on a prescribed smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian background $(M,g,T)$ of signature $(-+++)$, with $m>0$ a fixed primitive mass in kg and $c>0$ in m/s, adopt the stationary-action model

$$S_m[x]=-mc\int_I\sqrt{-g(x',x') }\,d\lambda.$$

Here λ is an increasing regular parameter, endpoint events are fixed, and admissible variations remain future timelike. The integrand is the proper-time length density, so $S_m=-mc^2\int d\tau$; its dimension is action (J s). The adopted premise concerns this ideal free test body only. It is neither a theorem about all matter nor an empirical report, and supplies no backreaction or completeness claim. The flat ideal-clock specialization agrees with [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]; adopting this action on a curved background remains a separate premise.

On a prescribed background $(M,g,T)$, adopt a distinct massless classical particle model with fields $x:I\to M$, $p(\lambda)\in T^*_{x(\lambda)}M$, and a positive smooth multiplier $e(\lambda)>0$:

$$S_0[x,p,e]=\int_I\left[p_a x'^a-eC_0(x,p)\right]d\lambda,\qquad C_0=\tfrac12g^{ab}p_ap_b.$$

Variations of $p,e$ are independent; the physical branch is $p\ne0$, $p^\sharp$ future null. With all spacetime coordinates measured in metres and dimensionless λ, $p_a$ has units kg m/s, $C_0$ has units kg²m²/s² and $e$ has units s/kg, making the action J s. Other parameter units scale $e$ accordingly. This is a separate adopted model: null curves have no proper-time parameter, the model does not arise by setting $m=0$ in $P=mU$, and its positive momentum scale is additional initial data. On the nonzero branch, the vertical differential is $d_pC_0=p^\sharp\ne0$: nondegeneracy of $g^{-1}$ and $p\ne0$ give $p^\sharp\ne0$. Hence the shell is a regular primary constraint in the sense of [[def-rpm-h-regular-constraint-system]]. This postulate is not an empirical observation or a deduction from the massive model.

The cotangent phase-space carrier convention assumes countable choice ACω only; full choice is not assumed.

Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold as in [[def-rpm-h-cotangent-phase-space]], and write its cotangent phase space in induced coordinates $(q^i,p_i)$. With $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$, define $X_H$ by $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$ and define the Poisson bracket by $\{F,G\}:=X_G(F)$. Then

$$X_H=\frac{\partial H}{\partial p_i}\frac{\partial}{\partial q^i}-\frac{\partial H}{\partial q^i}\frac{\partial}{\partial p_i},\qquad \{F,G\}=F_{q^i}G_{p_i}-F_{p_i}G_{q^i}.$$

The bracket is coordinate independent and makes smooth functions a Poisson algebra. If $H_t$ is smooth on an open time-dependent domain $D\subset\mathbb R\times T^*Q$, each solution of $\dot z=X_{H_t}(z)$ has local uniqueness and smooth dependence on initial data and parameters; on its actual interval,

$$\frac{d}{dt}F(t,z(t))=\partial_tF+\{F,H_t\}.$$

No completeness or global flow is asserted. If $H$ is smooth, each local time-$t$ flow map preserves ω.

Let $(M,g,T)$ be a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-+++)$. Work in a spacetime chart on a compact parameter interval $[a,b]$ with $a<b$; take $x,p,e$ smooth on a neighbourhood of that interval, $e>0$, and $m\ge0$. Restrict to the future shell branch: when $m>0$, $p^\sharp$ is future timelike; when $m=0$, require $p\ne0$ and $p^\sharp$ future null. Set $C_m=\tfrac12(g^{ab}p_ap_b+m^2c^2)$ and define the first-order functional

$$I_m[x,p,e]=\int_a^b\left(p_ax'^a-eC_m(x,p)\right)d\lambda.$$

Take independent smooth variations of $p,e$ and fixed-endpoint variations of $x$. Stationarity on the chart segment is equivalent to

$$x'^a=e g^{ab}p_b,\quad p'_a=-\tfrac e2\partial_a g^{bc}p_bp_c,\quad C_m=0.$$

On the massive future branch $m>0$, these equations are equivalent to stationary paths of the square-root action in [[post-rpm-h-free-test-particle-action]]; the mechanical covector is $p=mc\,x'^\flat/\sqrt{-g(x',x')}$, and proper-time gauge has $e=1/m$. For the separate nonzero future-null branch $m=0$, the equations describe a null geodesic with an arbitrary positive parameter multiplier; no proper-time parameter exists. In both cases the unparameterized path is a geodesic, and no existence or completeness claim is made.

In affine Minkowski space with inertial coordinates $x^0,x^i$ measured in metres and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, let $m\ge0$ and let

$$\Sigma_m^+=\{(x,p): -p_0=P^0=\sqrt{m^2c^2+|\mathbf p|^2},\ p_0<0\},$$

where $\mathbf p\ne0$ when $m=0$, and write $P^i=p_i$ for the spatial raised momentum components. The characteristic flow of the restricted canonical form is $(x,p)\mapsto(x+\alpha P,p)$, and its orbit space is globally diffeomorphic to $B_m=\mathbb R^3_a\times\mathbb R^3_p$ for $m>0$, or $\mathbb R^3_a\times(\mathbb R^3_p\setminus\{0\})$ for $m=0$, by

$$a^i=x^i-\frac{P^i}{P^0}x^0,\qquad p_i=p_i.$$

The reduced symplectic form is $da^i\wedge dp_i$. The quotient is Hausdorff and second countable and each full characteristic line meets each slice $x^0=ct$ exactly once. This is an explicit free flat quotient, not a conclusion about arbitrary first-class systems.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $n$. Its cotangent bundle is

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units $[F]$ and $[G]$ has units $[F][G]/(\text{action})$. These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. The use of $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ is exactly the use in the smooth cotangent-bundle suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ and let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold. A finite family of smooth functions $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ defined on an open neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ is a **regular primary constraint family** on

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units $[\chi_a]$, then $u^a$ has units energy divided by $[\chi_a]$, so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

Let $(P^{2n},\omega)$ be symplectic, and let $N=\{\chi_1=\cdots=\chi_r=0\}$ be a regular embedded level surface with $\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}=0$ on $N$. Then $\ker(\omega|_N)$ is exactly the rank-$r$ distribution spanned by the restricted Hamiltonian vector fields $X_{\chi_a}$. This distribution is involutive. Around every point of $N$, its leaves admit smooth Frobenius coordinates $(s^1,\ldots,s^r,y^1,\ldots,y^{2n-2r})$, and the local leaf space has a unique smooth closed nondegenerate two-form $\omega_{\mathrm{red}}$ whose pullback is $\omega|_N$. Thus regular first-class constraints yield a local symplectic quotient. No global orbit-space regularity follows from these hypotheses.

derivations.claim: The periodic quotient atlas makes $T^2$ a smooth manifold. By [F1], its cotangent form is $\omega=dx\wedge dp_x+dy\wedge dp_y$. The differential $dC=dp_x+a\,dp_y$ is nowhere zero, so $C^{-1}(0)$ is a regular embedded hypersurface. The canonical bracket is skew, hence $\{C,C\}=0$ and the single constraint is first class.
Contraction with $dx\wedge dp_x+dy\wedge dp_y$ gives $X_C=\partial_x+a\partial_y$. Integrating this constant vector field yields the stated flow and leaves momenta fixed.

Fix a starting point $(x_0,y_0)$ and any target first coordinate $u\in[0,1)$. For each $n\in\mathbb Z$, the flow parameter $s=n-x_0+u$ makes the first coordinate equal to $u$ modulo one and the second equal to $y_0+a(n-x_0+u)$ modulo one. The residues $na\bmod1$ are dense: for any integer $N\ge2$, divide $[0,1)$ into $N$ half-open intervals of length $1/N$. Two of the $N+1$ residues $0,a,\ldots,Na\bmod1$ lie in one interval, so for some nonzero integer $k$ and integer $r$ we have $0<\delta:=|ka-r|<1/N$; the strict lower bound follows from irrationality. Replacing $k$ by $-k$ if needed, $\delta$ is an integer multiple of $a$ modulo one. The residues $j\delta$ for $j=0,1,\ldots,\lfloor1/\delta\rfloor$ have gaps at most $\delta$ around the unit interval, so they form a $1/N$-net. Since $N$ is arbitrary, the multiples of $a$ are dense modulo one. Therefore the orbit is dense in the second coordinate for the chosen $u$; as $u$ was arbitrary, the flow orbit is dense in $T^2$.

The orbits through $(0,0,0,0)$ and $(0,1/2,0,0)$ are distinct: equality would require integers $n,k$ with $an+k=1/2$; if $n\ne0$ this would make $a$ rational, and if $n=0$ it would assert that an integer equals $1/2$. Both orbits are dense by step 3.1. Let $U$ be a saturated open subset of the constraint surface that meets the fixed-momentum torus. Its intersection with that torus is nonempty, open, and saturated. Its complement is closed and saturated; if nonempty, it contains a whole dense orbit and hence the whole torus. Therefore the intersection is the whole torus. Any quotient neighborhoods of the two distinct orbit classes have such preimages and therefore intersect, so the orbit space is non-Hausdorff. This does not contradict the local symplectic leaf spaces in [F3].

The claim is local to the invertible projection domain; it asserts no continuation after a caustic. $S$ has action units, so $[S]=\mathrm{J\,s}$, $[S_q]=[p]$, and $[S_t]=\mathrm J$ when $t,q,p,H$ use SI time, length, momentum, and energy units.

derivations.claim: Hamilton's equations from [L2] give $\dot p=0$, so $p(t,a)=S_0'(a)=-\kappa a$. Also $\dot q=E_p=c^2p/E$, hence integration with $q(0,a)=a$ gives the displayed formula.

Differentiate: $\partial_aq=1-t\kappa c^2\frac d{dp}(p/E)$. Since $E^2=m^2c^4+c^2p^2$, $\frac d{dp}(p/E)=m^2c^4/E^3$. Thus $\partial_aq=1-t\kappa m^2c^6/E^3$. Because $E\ge mc^2$, this is at least $1-t\kappa/m$, positive for $t<m/\kappa$. At $a=0$, $p=0$ and $E=mc^2$, so it equals zero at $t=m/\kappa$; this is the first singular point.

At that point $\partial_ap=-\kappa$. If a smooth graph $p=S_q(t,q(t,a))$ extended through it, the chain rule would give $\partial_ap=S_{qq}\partial_aq=0$, contradicting $-\kappa\ne0$. Hence no such smooth single-valued graph extension exists through that projection singularity.

Assume countable choice ACω, as in [[def-countable-choice]], for the smooth cotangent-bundle carrier convention used by this page; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Let $\mathcal D$ be an open subset of the time-dependent tangent bundle $\mathbb R\times TQ$ of a finite-dimensional smooth manifold $Q$, and let $L:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. For fixed $t$, the **fibre derivative** is the map

$$\mathbb F L(t,q,v)=(t,q,p),\qquad p(w)=\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}L(t,q,v+sw),$$

as in [[def-fibre-derivative-and-legendre-transform-of-a-lagrangian]]. In induced coordinates $p_i=\partial L/\partial v^i$.

The Lagrangian is **regular** at $(t,q,v)$ when the velocity Hessian $(\partial^2L/\partial v^i\partial v^j)$ is invertible there; regularity gives only a local inverse branch. It is **hyperregular on a declared domain** when $\mathbb F L$ is a diffeomorphism from that entire domain onto an open subset of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$.

It is **almost regular on a declared domain $\mathcal D_0\subseteq\mathcal D$** when the following are all assumed: $\mathbb F L|_{\mathcal D_0}$ has constant rank; its image $N$ is an embedded submanifold of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$; its corestriction $\mathcal D_0\to N$ is a surjective submersion (its differential is surjective at every point); and every fibre of that corestriction is connected. These hypotheses are not consequences of singularity alone.

The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units \([\chi_a]\), then $u^a$ has units energy divided by \([\chi_a]\), so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

Use the signature $(-,+,+,+)$ throughout. In the flat case, **Minkowski spacetime** means the affine model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]: $A$ is an affine space, $\eta$ is a nondegenerate Lorentz form on its four-dimensional displacement space, and $C^+$ selects the future cone. In the curved case, a **background spacetime** means a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the metric and time orientation are fixed data, not dynamical unknowns here. No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the smooth subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. In the flat model these are affine curves into $A$ with tangent in the selected future timelike or null cone from [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]].

An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** is a chosen orthonormal frame field, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.

For $x\in\mathbb R$, define
$$\sinh x:=\frac{\exp x-\exp(-x)}2,\qquad\cosh x:=\frac{\exp x+\exp(-x)}2,$$
$$\tanh x:=\frac{\sinh x}{\cosh x},\qquad\operatorname{sech}x:=\frac1{\cosh x}.$$
For $x\ne0$, define
$$\coth x:=\frac{\cosh x}{\sinh x},\qquad\operatorname{csch}x:=\frac1{\sinh x}.$$

The positivity of $\exp$ makes $\cosh x>0$ for every $x$. If $x\ne0$, then
$x\ne-x$, so strict increase of $\exp$ makes $\exp x\ne\exp(-x)$; hence
$\sinh x\ne0$. Thus all four quotients above are defined on exactly their
stated domains ([[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]],
[[thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing]]).

For all real $x,y$,
$$\sinh(x+y)=\sinh x\cosh y+\cosh x\sinh y,\qquad\cosh(x+y)=\cosh x\cosh y+\sinh x\sinh y,$$
$$\cosh^2x-\sinh^2x=1,\qquad(\sinh x)'=\cosh x,\qquad(\cosh x)'=\sinh x.$$
Moreover $\sinh:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is odd, strictly increasing, and onto;
$\cosh:\mathbb R\to[1,\infty)$ is even and positive, and its restriction
to $[0,\infty)$ is strictly increasing and onto $[1,\infty)$; and
$\tanh:\mathbb R\to(-1,1)$ is strictly increasing and onto. On their declared domains,
$$(\tanh x)'=\operatorname{sech}^2x,\quad(\coth x)'=-\operatorname{csch}^2x,\quad(\operatorname{sech}x)'=-\operatorname{sech}x\tanh x,\quad(\operatorname{csch}x)'=-\operatorname{csch}x\coth x.$$

The real exponential function is $C^\infty$, and for every $m\in\mathbb N$,
$$\exp^{(m)}=\exp.$$
In particular $(\exp)'=\exp$.

Let $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ with
$g[A] \subseteq B$ and let $f : B \to \mathbb{R}$, so that the composite
$f \circ g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined. Let $c \in A$ be a limit point of
$A$ ([[def-limit-point-r]]) at which $g$ is differentiable
([[def-derivative]]), put $b := g(c)$, and suppose $b$ is a limit point of $B$
at which $f$ is differentiable. Then $f \circ g$ is differentiable at $c$ and

$$(f \circ g)'(c) \;=\; f'\bigl(g(c)\bigr)\,g'(c) .$$

**Both limit-point hypotheses are needed, and neither is automatic.** That $c$
is a limit point of $A$ is what makes $g'(c)$ and $(f \circ g)'(c)$ defined
symbols; that $b = g(c)$ is a limit point of $B$ is what makes $f'(b)$ one.
Nothing forces the second: $g$ may be differentiable at $c$ and send $c$ to an
isolated point of $B$, and there $f'(b)$ is not defined and the formula asserts
nothing.

**No case analysis appears anywhere.** The naive difference-quotient proof
writes $\frac{f(g(x)) - f(g(c))}{g(x) - g(c)} \cdot \frac{g(x) - g(c)}{x - c}$
and then has to say what happens where $g(x) = g(c)$, which may occur at points
arbitrarily close to $c$. Carathéodory's factorisation never divides by the
inner increment, so the difficulty does not arise.

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $c \in A$ be a limit point of $A$
([[def-limit-point-r]]), let $f, g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at $c$
([[def-derivative]]) and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. Then:

1. $f + g$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(f+g)'(c) = f'(c) + g'(c)$;
2. $\alpha f$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(\alpha f)'(c) = \alpha f'(c)$;
3. $fg$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(fg)'(c) = f'(c)g(c) + f(c)g'(c)$;
4. if $g(c) \ne 0$ then, writing $A_0 := \{\, x \in A : g(x) \ne 0 \,\}$, the
   point $c$ lies in $A_0$ and is a limit point of $A_0$, the quotient
   $(f/g)|_{A_0} : A_0 \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \mapsto f(x)/g(x)$, is differentiable
   at $c$ as a function on $A_0$, and
   $$\bigl((f/g)|_{A_0}\bigr)'(c) \;=\; \frac{f'(c)\,g(c) - f(c)\,g'(c)}{g(c)^{2}} .$$

Each claim asserts two things: that the derivative on the left exists, and that
it has the stated value. Both are proved.

**Why claim 4 is stated on $A_0$.** The function $f/g$ is not defined where $g$
vanishes, and $g$ may vanish at points of $A$ far from $c$; restricting to $A_0$
is forced. That the restriction still has $c$ as a limit point, so that a
derivative there means anything at all, is not free either, and it is the last
claim of [[lem-sign-preservation-near-a-limit]] applied to $g$. The hypothesis
is $g(c) \ne 0$, not "$g$ vanishes nowhere".

**Everything is proved through
[[thm-caratheodory-characterisation]].** No difference quotient is estimated and
no limit theorem beyond continuity is used, so no choice principle is spent.
The four identities are four algebraic rearrangements of an increment, each
followed by a reading of [[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]].

Let $a < b$ be reals, let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be integrable
([[def-darboux-integral]]), let $F$ be its integral function
([[def-the-integral-function]]), and let $c \in [a,b]$ be a point at which $f$ is
continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]). Then $F$ is differentiable at $c$ as a
function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-derivative]]) and

$$F'(c) \;=\; f(c) .$$

At $c = a$ and $c = b$ this is the one-sided statement, which is what
[[def-derivative]] means at those points: every point of a nondegenerate interval
is a limit point of it, so $F'(c)$ is a meaningful symbol at every $c \in [a,b]$,
and the difference quotient is taken over $[a,b] \setminus \{c\}$.

**Consequently, if $f$ is continuous on the whole of $[a,b]$, then $F$ is a
primitive of $f$ there**: $F' = f$ at every point of $[a,b]$.

**Continuity at $c$ is a hypothesis and it cannot be dropped.** For an integrable
$f$ that is discontinuous at $c$, $F'(c)$ may fail to exist, and it may exist and
differ from $f(c)$; both are exhibited on the companion page, by
an integrable function with no primitive and by a false
statement about the integral function.

Let $a < b$ be reals and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[a,b]$
([[def-continuity-real]]). Then $f$ is bounded ([[def-bounded-set]]) and Riemann
integrable on $[a,b]$ ([[def-darboux-integral]]).

**The proof gives more than integrability: it gives a partition that works.** For
every real $\varepsilon > 0$ the uniform partition into $N$ parts already
satisfies $U(f,P) - L(f,P) < \varepsilon$, as soon as $N$ is large enough that
$(b-a)/\iota(N)$ is below the $\delta$ that uniform continuity supplies for
$\varepsilon/\bigl(2(b-a)\bigr)$. Uniform continuity is exactly what makes one
$\delta$ serve all $N$ subintervals at once, and it is the only place where the

$$\Pi_U{}^a{}_b:=\delta^a_b+\frac{U^aU_b}{c^2},\qquad f_0^a(x,U):=\alpha F^a{}_b(x)U^b,$$

Bilinearity gives $g(n,n)=-1$ and $g(n,N)=-\sqrt{-g(N,N)}<0$, so [F2] makes $n$ an observer at every point and hence a smooth observer congruence. This supplies an observer field without identifying it with a chart or tetrad.

Fix $p\in U$ and a connected chart around $p$. The four coordinate vectors form a basis at $p$. By [F2], the linear map $h_{n_p}$ has image the three-dimensional space $n_p^\perp$, so three projected coordinate vectors form a basis of $n_p^\perp$. Extend the chosen coordinate fields over the chart and project them by $h_n$; after shrinking the chart, their projections remain independent by continuity. They lie in the positive-definite rest spaces by [F2]. Apply the three finite Gram-Schmidt operations in these rest spaces; every denominator is the positive square root of a positive smooth squared norm, so [F5] makes the resulting fields smooth. Together with $E_0=n$, the three fields form a local tetrad. If needed, reverse one spatial member so the tetrad has the supplied orientation from [F1]; the sign remains fixed on the connected chart. This is a local tetrad field as in [F3], not a coordinate frame or an assertion of an adapted coordinate chart. Thus an $n$-adapted tetrad exists locally, with no global tetrad or hypersurface-orthogonality conclusion.

In a length-coordinate chart, each first coordinate derivative of $g_{ab}$ has dimension $\mathrm m^{-1}$, so the Christoffel formula in [F4] has dimension $\mathrm m^{-1}$. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ and let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold. A finite family of smooth functions $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ defined on an open neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ is a **regular primary constraint family** on

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units \([\chi_a]\), then $u^a$ has units energy divided by \([\chi_a]\), so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

At $\Phi(L)=\eta$, its derivative is $D\Phi_L(\Delta)=\Delta^T\eta L+L^T\eta\Delta$. For any symmetric $S$, set $\Delta=L\eta^{-1}S/2$; using $L^T\eta L=\eta$ and $S^T=S$, each summand equals $S/2$. Thus $D\Phi_L$ is onto.

Every point of $\Phi^{-1}(\eta)$ is regular by step 1.1, and the level is nonempty because it contains $I$. Thus [F3] makes $O(1,3)=\Phi^{-1}(\eta)$ an embedded six-dimensional submanifold of $GL(4,\mathbb R)$. For $L\in O(1,3)$, $Le_0$ is timelike and $L$ is a homeomorphism of the timelike set; [F4] implies that $L$ preserves the selected future component exactly when $Le_0$ lies in that component. Since $e_0$ is the positive time-axis vector, this is exactly $L^0{}_0>0$. Also $|L^0{}_0|\ge1$, and taking determinants in $L^T\eta L=\eta$ gives $(\det L)^2=1$. Therefore $\det L=1$ and $L^0{}_0>0$ select an open subset of $O(1,3)$. By [F1] this subset is $SO^+(1,3)$. Matrix multiplication and inversion restrict smoothly from $GL(4)$, so this subgroup is a six-dimensional Lie group.

Give $G=\mathbb R^4\times SO^+(1,3)$ the product manifold structure from step 2.1 and multiplication $(a,\Lambda)(b,L)=(a+\Lambda b,\Lambda L)$. Both parenthesizations of a triple product equal $(a+\Lambda b+\Lambda Lc,\Lambda LM)$; the identity is $(0,I)$; and direct substitution shows $(-\Lambda^{-1}a,\Lambda^{-1})$ is a left and right inverse. Multiplication and inversion are smooth because matrix multiplication and inversion on $SO^+(1,3)$ are smooth and the translation operations are smooth. The affine matrix map $\rho(a,\Lambda)=\begin{pmatrix}\Lambda&a\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ is injective, has smooth inverse onto its image by block projection, and is a group homomorphism because matrix multiplication gives $\rho(a+\Lambda b,\Lambda L)$. The product manifold tangent at identity is $\mathbb R^4\times T_I SO^+(1,3)$. By [F5], the latter tangent space is contained in the six-dimensional space of matrices satisfying $A^T\eta+\eta A=0$; both have dimension six by step 2.1 and [F5], so they are equal. Hence $d\rho_I(a,A)=\begin{pmatrix}A&a\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$. A group homomorphism carries left-invariant vector fields to related left-invariant fields: differentiating $\rho\circ L_g=L_{\rho(g)}\circ\rho$ gives this relation. Related fields' brackets are related, since applying each bracket to a smooth test function and expanding $X(Yf)-Y(Xf)$ gives the same identity after composition with $\rho$. For matrices $M,N$, the left-invariant fields on $GL(5)$ are $g\mapsto gM$ and $g\mapsto gN$; differentiating these fields gives their commutator at the identity as $MN-NM$. Thus the bracket of two pair matrices is $\begin{pmatrix}[A,B]&Ab-Ba\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, yielding $[(a,A),(b,B)]=(Ab-Ba,[A,B])$.

The cotangent lift preserves the covector-tangent pairing: $p'(dx')=(\Lambda^{-T}p)(\Lambda dx)=p(dx)$. unresolved_inputs.actual_statement_excerpt:
Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $n$. Its cotangent bundle is

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units \([F]\) and \([G]\) has units \([F][G]/(\text{action})\). These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. The use of $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ is exactly the use in the smooth cotangent-bundle suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

citations.quote: There is a unique smooth bundle map $\star_g:\Omega^k(M)\to\Omega^{4-k}(M)$ characterized by $$\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$$ at every point.

For $\omega\in\Omega^k(M)$, define the candidate $d\omega$ on smooth vector fields by $$d\omega(X_0,\ldots,X_k)=\sum_i(-1)^iX_i\omega(X_0,\widehat X_i,\ldots,X_k)+\sum_{i<j}(-1)^{i+j}\omega([X_i,X_j],X_0,\widehat X_i,\widehat X_j,\ldots,X_k).$$ The next lemma proves that this candidate is a form.
Summing over increasing $k$-tuples $I$, and writing $dx^I=dx^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{i_k}$, if $\omega=\sum_I\omega_I\,dx^I$, then $$d\omega=\sum_I d\omega_I\wedge dx^I.$$
The graded vector space $$ \Omega^*(M):=\bigoplus_{k\ge 0}\Omega^k(M) $$ with the wedge product is an associative graded-commutative algebra.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form $$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$ It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if $g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$, so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

citations.quote:
Let $a < b$ be reals, let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be integrable
([[def-darboux-integral]]), let $F$ be its integral function
([[def-the-integral-function]]), and let $c \in [a,b]$ be a point at which $f$ is
continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]). Then $F$ is differentiable at $c$ as a
function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-derivative]]) and

$$F'(c) \;=\; f(c) .$$

At $c = a$ and $c = b$ this is the one-sided statement, which is what
[[def-derivative]] means at those points: every point of a nondegenerate interval
is a limit point of it, so $F'(c)$ is a meaningful symbol at every $c \in [a,b]$,
and the difference quotient is taken over $[a,b] \setminus \{c\}$.

**Consequently, if $f$ is continuous on the whole of $[a,b]$, then $F$ is a
primitive of $f$ there**: $F' = f$ at every point of $[a,b]$.

**Continuity at $c$ is a hypothesis and it cannot be dropped.** For an integrable
$f$ that is discontinuous at $c$, $F'(c)$ may fail to exist, and it may exist and
differ from $f(c)$; both are exhibited on the companion page, by
an integrable function with no primitive and by a false
statement about the integral function.

Let $a < b$ be reals and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[a,b]$
([[def-continuity-real]]). Then $f$ is bounded ([[def-bounded-set]]) and Riemann
integrable on $[a,b]$ ([[def-darboux-integral]]).

**The proof gives more than integrability: it gives a partition that works.** For
every real $\varepsilon > 0$ the uniform partition into $N$ parts already
satisfies $U(f,P) - L(f,P) < \varepsilon$, as soon as $N$ is large enough that
$(b-a)/\iota(N)$ is below the $\delta$ that uniform continuity supplies for
$\varepsilon/\bigl(2(b-a)\bigr)$. Uniform continuity is exactly what makes one
$\delta$ serve all $N$ subintervals at once, and it is the only place where the
compactness of $[a,b]$ is used.

The real exponential function is $C^\infty$, and for every $m\in\mathbb N$,
$$\exp^{(m)}=\exp.$$
In particular $(\exp)'=\exp$.

Let $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ with
$g[A] \subseteq B$ and let $f : B \to \mathbb{R}$, so that the composite
$f \circ g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined. Let $c \in A$ be a limit point of
$A$ ([[def-limit-point-r]]) at which $g$ is differentiable
([[def-derivative]]), put $b := g(c)$, and suppose $b$ is a limit point of $B$
at which $f$ is differentiable. Then $f \circ g$ is differentiable at $c$ and

$$(f \circ g)'(c) \;=\; f'\bigl(g(c)\bigr)\,g'(c) .$$

**Both limit-point hypotheses are needed, and neither is automatic.** That $c$
is a limit point of $A$ is what makes $g'(c)$ and $(f \circ g)'(c)$ defined
symbols; that $b = g(c)$ is a limit point of $B$ is what makes $f'(b)$ one.
Nothing forces the second: $g$ may be differentiable at $c$ and send $c$ to an
isolated point of $B$, and there $f'(b)$ is not defined and the formula asserts
nothing.

**No case analysis appears anywhere.** The naive difference-quotient proof
writes $\frac{f(g(x)) - f(g(c))}{g(x) - g(c)} \cdot \frac{g(x) - g(c)}{x - c}$
and then has to say what happens where $g(x) = g(c)$, which may occur at points
arbitrarily close to $c$. Carathéodory's factorisation never divides by the
inner increment, so the difficulty does not arise.

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $c \in A$ be a limit point of $A$
([[def-limit-point-r]]), let $f, g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at $c$
([[def-derivative]]) and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. Then:

1. $f + g$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(f+g)'(c) = f'(c) + g'(c)$;
2. $\alpha f$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(\alpha f)'(c) = \alpha f'(c)$;
3. $fg$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(fg)'(c) = f'(c)g(c) + f(c)g'(c)$;
4. if $g(c) \ne 0$ then, writing $A_0 := \{\, x \in A : g(x) \ne 0 \,\}$, the
   point $c$ lies in $A_0$ and is a limit point of $A_0$, the quotient
   $(f/g)|_{A_0} : A_0 \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \mapsto f(x)/g(x)$, is differentiable
   at $c$ as a function on $A_0$, and
   $$\bigl((f/g)|_{A_0}\bigr)'(c) \;=\; \frac{f'(c)\,g(c) - f(c)\,g'(c)}{g(c)^{2}} .$$

Each claim asserts two things: that the derivative on the left exists, and that
it has the stated value. Both are proved.

**Why claim 4 is stated on $A_0$.** The function $f/g$ is not defined where $g$
vanishes, and $g$ may vanish at points of $A$ far from $c$; restricting to $A_0$
is forced. That the restriction still has $c$ as a limit point, so that a
derivative there means anything at all, is not free either, and it is the last
claim of [[lem-sign-preservation-near-a-limit]] applied to $g$. The hypothesis
is $g(c) \ne 0$, not "$g$ vanishes nowhere".

**Everything is proved through
[[thm-caratheodory-characterisation]].** No difference quotient is estimated and
no limit theorem beyond continuity is used, so no choice principle is spent.
The four identities are four algebraic rearrangements of an increment, each
followed by a reading of [[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]].

Let $a < b$ be reals and let $f, g : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be integrable
([[def-darboux-integral]]). Then:

1. **Nonnegativity.** If $f(x) \ge 0$ for every $x \in [a,b]$ then
   $\int_a^b f \ge 0$.
2. **Monotonicity.** If $f(x) \le g(x)$ for every $x \in [a,b]$ then
   $$\int_a^b f \;\le\; \int_a^b g .$$
3. **Two-sided bound.** If $m \le f(x) \le M$ for every $x \in [a,b]$, with
   $m, M$ real, then
   $$m\,(b-a) \;\le\; \int_a^b f \;\le\; M\,(b-a) .$$

**Equality in claim 1 does not force $f$ to vanish.** A nonnegative integrable
function with integral $0$ may be positive at infinitely many points; that is
[[fs-nonnegative-integrable-with-zero-integral-vanishes]] on the previous page's
companion. Under the additional hypothesis of continuity the conclusion does
hold, and that is [[thm-nonnegative-continuous-with-zero-integral-vanishes]]
below.

**Claim 2 is stated for $a < b$ and is not orientation-invariant.** With the
convention of [[def-oriented-integral]], $f \le g$ gives
$\int_u^v f \le \int_u^v g$ when $u \le v$ and the reverse inequality when
$u \ge v$, since both sides change sign together.

Let $a < b$ be reals and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy

$$m \;\le\; f(x) \;\le\; M \qquad \text{for every } x \in [a,b],$$

with $m, M$ real. Then $f$ is bounded ([[def-bounded-set]]), so its Darboux sums
and integrals are defined ([[def-darboux-sums]], [[def-darboux-integral]]), and
for **every** partition $P$ of $[a,b]$ ([[def-partition-and-refinement]])

$$m(b-a) \;\le\; L(f,P) \;\le\; \underline{\int_a^b} f \;\le\; \overline{\int_a^b} f \;\le\; U(f,P) \;\le\; M(b-a) .$$

In particular, taking $f$ to be the constant function with value $c$:

$$\int_a^b c \;=\; c\,(b-a) ,$$

the constant function being integrable, with $L(f,P) = U(f,P) = c(b-a)$ for
every partition $P$.

For every real $x$, $\exp(x)>0$ and
$$\exp(-x)=\frac1{\exp(x)}.$$

Let $(X,d)$ be a nonempty compact metric space ([[def-metric-compactness]],
[[def-metric-space]]) and let $f : X \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous
([[def-metric-continuity]]), $\mathbb{R}$ carrying its usual metric
$d_{\mathbb{R}}(s,t) = |s-t|$ ([[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]]). Then the
image $f[X]$ is bounded above and below ([[def-bounded-set]]), and it has a
maximum and a minimum ([[def-max-min]]): there are points
$x_{\max}, x_{\min} \in X$ with

$$f(x_{\min}) \;\le\; f(x) \;\le\; f(x_{\max}) \qquad \text{for every } x \in X,$$

and then $f(x_{\max}) = \sup f[X]$ and $f(x_{\min}) = \inf f[X]$
([[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[def-infimum]]).

Nonemptiness of $X$ is a hypothesis and not an oversight: for $X = \emptyset$ the
image is empty and has neither a supremum nor a maximum. No choice principle is
used.

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ ([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
([[def-derivative]]). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the cotangent/HJ supplier chain. Let $H(t,q,p)$ be smooth and let $S(t,q,\alpha)$ be a $C^3$ solution of $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$ on an open domain. If the mixed matrix $S_{q\alpha}$ is invertible at $(t,q,\alpha)$, then after restricting neighborhoods the equations $p=S_q$, $\beta=S_\alpha$ define a local canonical transformation $(q,p)\leftrightarrow(\alpha,\beta)$ at each fixed $t$, and $\beta$ is constant along its Hamilton characteristics. Such a family is a complete integral only on that nonsingular local domain. In a temporal spacetime chart satisfying H9, the covariant future-shell equation $g^{ab}S_aS_b+m^2c^2=0$ reduces to the time Hamilton–Jacobi equation with $p_0=S_t/c=-H/c$; for $m=0$ require a nonzero future null covector. The function $S$ has action units, not dimensionless phase units.

In affine Minkowski space with $x^0=ct$, let $m\ge0$, $p_i$ be spatial momentum components and $p_i\ne0$ for $m=0$. On the future shell, $p_0=-E/c$, where

$$E(\mathbf p)=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\mathbf p|^2}.$$

On any compact interval $J=[t_1,t_2]$ of inertial time, the gauge $x^0=ct$ reduces the first-order shell action to

$$I_J=\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\left(p_i\dot q^i-E(\mathbf p)\right)dt,\qquad q^i=x^i.$$

The gauge pair $C_m=0$, $\psi=x^0-ct=0$ is second class because $\{C_m,\psi\}=-P^0\ne0$ on the future shell; its Dirac reduction gives the canonical spatial bracket. The reduced Hamilton equations are $\dot q^i=c^2p_i/E$, $\dot p_i=0$, agreeing with the unreduced characteristic trajectories. On this full flat future shell every characteristic line meets each inertial-time slice once; this global assertion does not extend by this proof to a curved temporal chart.

derivations.claim: Differentiation gives $S_q=\alpha$, $S_t=-E(\alpha)$, and hence $S_t+E(S_q)=0$. Also $S_{q_i\alpha_j}=\delta_{ij}$, so its determinant is one. By [L1] this nonsingular family supplies local canonical integration coordinates on the stated domain.

Differentiating $E$ gives $\partial_{\alpha_i}E=c^2\alpha_i/E$ wherever $E>0$. Thus $\beta=S_\alpha=q-tc^2\alpha/E$ and rearranging yields the stated trajectory formula. For $m=0$, $E=c|\alpha|>0$ and differentiability requires $\alpha\ne0$, which is exactly the given domain.

The products $q\cdot\alpha$ and $tE$ have action units, while $\alpha$ is momentum and $\partial_\alpha S$ is length. Hence the generating function and canonical coordinates have the claimed physical dimensions.

Assume countable choice ACω, as in [[def-countable-choice]], for the smooth cotangent-bundle carrier convention used by this page; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Let $\mathcal D$ be an open subset of the time-dependent tangent bundle $\mathbb R\times TQ$ of a finite-dimensional smooth manifold $Q$, and let $L:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. For fixed $t$, the **fibre derivative** is the map

$$\mathbb F L(t,q,v)=(t,q,p),\qquad p(w)=\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}L(t,q,v+sw),$$

as in [[def-fibre-derivative-and-legendre-transform-of-a-lagrangian]]. In induced coordinates $p_i=\partial L/\partial v^i$.

The Lagrangian is **regular** at $(t,q,v)$ when the velocity Hessian $(\partial^2L/\partial v^i\partial v^j)$ is invertible there; regularity gives only a local inverse branch. It is **hyperregular on a declared domain** when $\mathbb F L$ is a diffeomorphism from that entire domain onto an open subset of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$.

It is **almost regular on a declared domain $\mathcal D_0\subseteq\mathcal D$** when the following are all assumed: $\mathbb F L|_{\mathcal D_0}$ has constant rank; its image $N$ is an embedded submanifold of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$; its corestriction $\mathcal D_0\to N$ is a surjective submersion (its differential is surjective at every point); and every fibre of that corestriction is connected. These hypotheses are not consequences of singularity alone.

They are parameters of the adopted physical formulation, not quantities derived by this definition. $$E_n(p):=-c\,p(n),\qquad q_n(p):=p+p(n)n^\flat,$$

where $n^\flat=g(n,\cdot)$. The restriction of $g^{-1}$ to covectors annihilating $n$ is positive definite, so it supplies the norm of $q_n(p)$. Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $n$. Its cotangent bundle is

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units \([F]\) and \([G]\) has units \([F][G]/(\text{action})\). These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. The use of $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ is exactly the use in the smooth cotangent-bundle suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ and let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold. A finite family of smooth functions $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ defined on an open neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ is a **regular primary constraint family** on

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units \([\chi_a]\), then $u^a$ has units energy divided by \([\chi_a]\), so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

Use the signature $(-,+,+,+)$ throughout. In the flat case, **Minkowski spacetime** means the affine model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]: $A$ is an affine space, $\eta$ is a nondegenerate Lorentz form on its four-dimensional displacement space, and $C^+$ selects the future cone. In the curved case, a **background spacetime** means a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the metric and time orientation are fixed data, not dynamical unknowns here. No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the smooth subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. In the flat model these are affine curves into $A$ with tangent in the selected future timelike or null cone from [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]].

An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** is a chosen orthonormal frame field, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume countable choice ACω, as in [[def-countable-choice]], for the smooth cotangent-bundle carrier convention used by this page; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Let $(M,g,T)$ be a smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-+++)$, with the geometric meaning fixed by [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Here $T$ denotes the future-cone field called $N$ in that definition. A **temporal product chart** is a smooth coordinate map from an open product $I\times\Omega\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$ onto an open subset of $M$, with coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$. We require $x^0$ to have length units and each $x^i$ to have length units in the physical interpretation.

The chart has **lapse-shift data** $(N,\beta,h)$ when $N:I\times\Omega\to(0,\infty)$, $\beta^i:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $h_{ij}:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$ are smooth, $h_{ij}=h_{ji}$, and the matrix $(h_{ij})$ is positive definite at each point, with

$$g=-N^2(dx^0)^2+h_{ij}(dx^i+\beta^i dx^0)(dx^j+\beta^j dx^0).$$

Write $h^{ij}$ for the inverse matrix. The normal field is

$$n=N^{-1}(\partial_0-\beta^i\partial_i).$$

Direct contraction gives $g(n,n)=-1$; require that $n$ is future-directed in the supplied time orientation. This field of observers is distinct from the coordinate vector $\partial_0$, which may be spacelike. The coefficients $N,\beta^i,h_{ij}$ are dimensionless when all four coordinates are in metres. This definition is local to the specified product chart; it asserts no global temporal foliation.

Let $m\ge0$ and $c>0$. Assume a temporal product chart with lapse-shift data $(N,\beta,h)$ as in [[def-rpm-h-temporal-chart-data]], all four coordinates measured in metres. On the future shell $C_m=\tfrac12(g^{ab}p_ap_b+m^2c^2)=0$, define

$$\kappa=\sqrt{m^2c^2+h^{ij}p_ip_j},\quad p_0=\beta^ip_i-N\kappa,\quad H(t,q,p)=-cp_0=c(N\kappa-\beta^ip_i).$$

For $m=0$, require $p_i\ne0$. On any compact interval $J=[t_1,t_2]$ whose path stays in the chart, the gauge $x^0=ct$ reduces the first-order action to $\int_{t_1}^{t_2}(p_i\dot q^i-H)dt$, and its variational equations on the interior of $J$ are exactly $\dot q^i=H_{p_i}$, $\dot p_i=-H_{q^i}$. The construction is local to this chart and intervals transverse to its time slices; no global curved-space gauge or quotient is asserted.

Assume countable choice ACω, as in [[def-countable-choice]], for the smooth cotangent-bundle carrier convention used by this page; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Fix a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,T)$ with signature $(-+++)$, as in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Here $T$ denotes the supplied smooth timelike field selecting the future cone, called $N$ in that geometric definition. Use the distinction among a spacetime, a worldline, a pointwise observer, an observer congruence, a tetrad and a chart given in [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. This definition does not make $g$ dynamical.

In this relativistic-particle model, $m>0$ is a fixed **primitive mass parameter** measured in kilograms, and $c>0$ is a fixed **primitive conversion parameter** measured in metres per second. They are parameters of the adopted physical formulation, not quantities derived by this definition. Coordinates $x^a$ in an SI chart have length units; a cotangent vector $p=p_a\,dx^a$ has units of momentum, $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, when all four coordinates are in metres. The canonical one-form $p_a\,dx^a$ therefore has action units $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Along a future-directed timelike curve with tangent $V=dx/d\lambda$, set $s:=\sqrt{-g(V,V)}$; then $d\tau=s\,d\lambda/c$, independently of the increasing regular parameter. The length action $-mc\int s\,d\lambda$ has action units. For a future unit observer $n$ and future causal covector $p$, define the model normal-observer energy and spatial momentum covector by

$$E_n(p):=-c\,p(n),\qquad q_n(p):=p+p(n)n^\flat,$$

where $n^\flat=g(n,\cdot)$. The restriction of $g^{-1}$ to covectors annihilating $n$ is positive definite, so it supplies the norm of $q_n(p)$. These are quantity definitions and unit conventions; they do not identify canonical momentum with mechanical momentum, assert that an apparatus measured these values, or establish a dynamical law.

derivations.claim: Use the inherited smooth bundle structure under [A1] and the temporal-chart data [F1]. The coordinate transformation is invertible with determinant one and pulls back the Minkowski line element $-(dX^0)^2+(dX^1)^2+(dX^2)^2+(dX^3)^2$ to $g$, proving flatness. The lapse is positive and $h=\delta$ is positive definite, so the chart satisfies [F1]; $\partial_0$ is spacelike since $g(\partial_0,\partial_0)=-1+4=3>0$, while $dx^0$ is temporal.
Here $\kappa=\sqrt{m^2c^2+p_1^2}$, so [F2] gives $H=c(\kappa-2p_1)$. The inequality $p_1>mc/\sqrt3$ implies $m^2c^2<3p_1^2$, hence $\kappa^2=m^2c^2+p_1^2<4p_1^2$, so $\kappa<2p_1$ and $H<0$.

Here $n=\partial_0-2\partial_1$, so $p(n)=p_0-2p_1=-\kappa$ on the future root; [F3] gives $E_n=-cp(n)=c\kappa>0$. The shell velocity formula gives $|w|_h=p_1/\kappa<1$, since $m>0$. The coordinate equation from [F2] gives $\dot q^1/c=p_1/\kappa-2$; because $\kappa^2<4p_1^2$, $p_1/\kappa>1/2$, so $2-p_1/\kappa>1$. Thus coordinate speed has magnitude greater than $c$ while local observer speed is less than $c$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $(P,\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold with its induced Poisson bracket, and let $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ be a regular constraint family on a common zero surface $N=\{z:\chi_a(z)=0\}$ as defined by [[def-rpm-h-regular-constraint-system]]. The family is **first-class on $N$** when

$$\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}(z)=0\qquad\text{for every }z\in N\text{ and all }a,b.$$

Equivalently, each pairwise bracket is weakly zero in the notation $F\approx0$ of [[def-rpm-h-regular-constraint-system]]. The Poisson bracket convention is that of [[thm-rpm-h-canonical-poisson-and-flow]]. This definition is a pointwise closure condition on the stated regular surface; it does not assert multiplier-algorithm termination or global quotient regularity.

Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold as in [[def-rpm-h-cotangent-phase-space]], and write its cotangent phase space in induced coordinates $(q^i,p_i)$. With $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$, define $X_H$ by $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$ and define the Poisson bracket by $\{F,G\}:=X_G(F)$. Then

$$X_H=\frac{\partial H}{\partial p_i}\frac{\partial}{\partial q^i}-\frac{\partial H}{\partial q^i}\frac{\partial}{\partial p_i},\qquad \{F,G\}=F_{q^i}G_{p_i}-F_{p_i}G_{q^i}.$$

The bracket is coordinate independent and makes smooth functions a Poisson algebra. If $H_t$ is smooth on an open time-dependent domain $D\subset\mathbb R\times T^*Q$, each solution of $\dot z=X_{H_t}(z)$ has local uniqueness and smooth dependence on initial data and parameters; on its actual interval,

$$\frac{d}{dt}F(t,z(t))=\partial_tF+\{F,H_t\}.$$

No completeness or global flow is asserted. If $H$ is smooth, each local time-$t$ flow map preserves ω.

Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be an open interval and $(P,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold. Let $\chi_a:I\times P\to\mathbb R$ be smooth and suppose the covectors $d_z\chi_a(\lambda,z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in N_\lambda:=\{z:\chi_1(\lambda,z)=\cdots=\chi_r(\lambda,z)=0\}$; this is the regular constraint condition of [[def-rpm-h-regular-constraint-system]] on each slice. Let $H_c:I\times P\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth ambient extension of a specified descended Hamiltonian. Work in a Darboux chart with coordinates $(q^i,p_i)$ and local potential $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$, so $d\theta=-\omega$ under the convention $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$; paths stay in this chart.
For any compact interval $[a,b]\subset I$ with $a<b$, paths $z:[a,b]\to P$ that stay in the chart and smooth multipliers $u^a:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ have action

$$I[z,u]=\int_a^b\left[\theta(\dot z)-H_c(\lambda,z)-u^a(\lambda)\chi_a(\lambda,z)\right]d\lambda.$$

Fixed-endpoint variations of $z$ and unrestricted variations of $u$ imply $z(\lambda)\in N_\lambda$ and $\dot z=X_{H_c(\lambda,\cdot)}+u^a(\lambda)X_{\chi_a(\lambda,\cdot)}$. A trajectory remains in the moving level set only when

$$\partial_\lambda\chi_a+\{\chi_a,H_c(\lambda,\cdot)\}+u^b(\lambda)\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}=0\quad\text{on }N_\lambda.$$

For constraints independent of $\lambda$, the first term is zero.

derivations.claim: The potential derivatives are $\partial_{x_1^a}V=2V'(r^2)r_a$ and $\partial_{x_2^a}V=-2V'(r^2)r_a$. The kinetic terms have $\partial_{p_i^a}C_i=P_i^a$. In $\{C_1,C_2\}$, the first particle contributes $-P_1^a(2V'r_a)$ and the second contributes $(-2V'r_a)P_2^a$; all other cross terms vanish. Their sum is the displayed bracket.

Choose $r=(0,R,0,0)$ with $R>0$, $V(z)=\lambda z$, and $\lambda>0$. Let $P_i^1=u_i>0$, other spatial components zero, and $P_i^0=\sqrt{m_i^2c^2+2\lambda R^2+u_i^2}$. Then $p_i^2=-(P_i^0)^2+u_i^2=-m_i^2c^2-2\lambda R^2$, so both $C_i=0$, while $r\cdot(P_1+P_2)=R(u_1+u_2)>0$. Each constraint differential has nonzero momentum component $P_i$ in its own cotangent factor, so $dC_1,dC_2$ are independent at this witness. Independence persists on a sufficiently small neighborhood, making the local joint level regular. The bracket is $\{C_1,C_2\}=-2\lambda R(u_1+u_2)\ne0$ there, so [F1] says the pair is not first-class on that local regular surface. With autonomous constraints and $H_c=0$, [L1] gives $\dot C_1=u^2\{C_1,C_2\}$ and $\dot C_2=u^1\{C_2,C_1\}$; hence preserving both constraints at this point forces $u^1=u^2=0$. Thus arbitrary independent nonzero multipliers need not preserve the joint surface.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $n$. Its cotangent bundle is

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units \([F]\) and \([G]\) has units \([F][G]/(\text{action})\). These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. The use of $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ is exactly the use in the smooth cotangent-bundle suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ and let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold. A finite family of smooth functions $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ defined on an open neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ is a **regular primary constraint family** on

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units \([\chi_a]\), then $u^a$ has units energy divided by \([\chi_a]\), so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold as in [[def-rpm-h-cotangent-phase-space]], and write its cotangent phase space in induced coordinates $(q^i,p_i)$. With $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$, define $X_H$ by $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$ and define the Poisson bracket by $\{F,G\}:=X_G(F)$. Then

$$X_H=\frac{\partial H}{\partial p_i}\frac{\partial}{\partial q^i}-\frac{\partial H}{\partial q^i}\frac{\partial}{\partial p_i},\qquad \{F,G\}=F_{q^i}G_{p_i}-F_{p_i}G_{q^i}.$$

The bracket is coordinate independent and makes smooth functions a Poisson algebra. If $H_t$ is smooth on an open time-dependent domain $D\subset\mathbb R\times T^*Q$, each solution of $\dot z=X_{H_t}(z)$ has local uniqueness and smooth dependence on initial data and parameters; on its actual interval,

$$\frac{d}{dt}F(t,z(t))=\partial_tF+\{F,H_t\}.$$

No completeness or global flow is asserted. If $H$ is smooth, each local time-$t$ flow map preserves ω.

Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be an open interval and $(P,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold. Let $\chi_a:I\times P\to\mathbb R$ be smooth and suppose the covectors $d_z\chi_a(\lambda,z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in N_\lambda:=\{z:\chi_1(\lambda,z)=\cdots=\chi_r(\lambda,z)=0\}$; this is the regular constraint condition of [[def-rpm-h-regular-constraint-system]] on each slice. Let $H_c:I\times P\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth ambient extension of a specified descended Hamiltonian. Work in a Darboux chart with coordinates $(q^i,p_i)$ and local potential $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$, so $d\theta=-\omega$ under the convention $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$; paths stay in this chart.
For any compact interval $[a,b]\subset I$ with $a<b$, paths $z:[a,b]\to P$ that stay in the chart and smooth multipliers $u^a:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ have action

$$I[z,u]=\int_a^b\left[\theta(\dot z)-H_c(\lambda,z)-u^a(\lambda)\chi_a(\lambda,z)\right]d\lambda.$$

Fixed-endpoint variations of $z$ and unrestricted variations of $u$ imply $z(\lambda)\in N_\lambda$ and $\dot z=X_{H_c(\lambda,\cdot)}+u^a(\lambda)X_{\chi_a(\lambda,\cdot)}$. A trajectory remains in the moving level set only when

$$\partial_\lambda\chi_a+\{\chi_a,H_c(\lambda,\cdot)\}+u^b(\lambda)\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}=0\quad\text{on }N_\lambda.$$

For constraints independent of $\lambda$, the first term is zero.
